To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the role of the proofreader of student writing is perceived to be that of a helper, a cleaner, a leveller, a mediator, and a teacher.
'proofreaders' conceptualisations of the role they perform are diverse, but they all have a pedagogical dimension'.
the proofreaders in this study conceptualize their roles as cleaners, helpers, mediators and/or teachers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a particular group of people who have a role in the assessment of students' written work.
the ways in which proofreaders of students' assessed work conceptualise their role, and the implications of these conceptualisations for their practice.
the nature of feedback in higher education.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
proofreading is a multifunctional role, and that the proofreader is not a 'cleaner'.
'proofreading' is not a simple process.
the role of proofreading is a complex, multi-faceted and dynamic one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the role of the proofreader is a complex one.
the role of a proofreader is a complex one, which involves a number of different functions, including the role of a teacher.
the role of the proofreader is not well defined, and that there is a need for further work to be undertaken to explore the impact of proofreaders' interventions on students' writing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
proofreading is not just an activity that can be carried out in a mechanical way.
proofreading is not a simple task, and that it is not a neutral one.
proofreaders' role is not limited to the correction of errors and that they can play a more active part in the learning process of students.
